guion_largo.texto:
This walk takes you to the eastern complex, the eastern part of the city.

According to INAH Lugares, there is a rectangular building with a sunken courtyard, a courtyard with three pyramidal platforms and a ball court. The Ramp of the Animals is also there, connecting with that court.

The INAH guide speaks of three temples, the ramp and the Temple of the Architects, also called the Sunken Courtyard. That is, it is a complex with several buildings grouped together.

As you walk, notice how the landscape changes. According to INAH Lugares, the city occupied six low hills, with terraces and retaining walls. That means every path climbs, descends and goes around the hills. A retaining wall is one that holds up the earth of a terrace so that it does not slide.

UNESCO considers that Xochicalco had three levels: a low one, a middle one and a high one. According to Hirth, the city grew very fast around the year six hundred and relocated between ten thousand and fifteen thousand people.

The next stops take place in that area. There is no need to hurry.

texto.pregunta: Myth: Xochicalco occupies a single hill.
texto.respuesta: Reality: According to INAH Lugares, it occupied six low hills, with terraces and walls.
